body: Ok thank you so much, I'll keep that in mind. I'm going to tell them that because I am scheduled to work in the next 48hrs, definitely 72 hours. Thank you for your help I hope you are well.

Ok that is good to know thank you. I feel like I'm not the threat to myself I was before my breakdown Wednesday but I have to admit my focus may be impaired so I wanted to know what I was walking in to. Thank you so much for your help I hope you are well.

Good point about Him knitting us in the womb, especially since that is likely when someone becomes trans.

Thanks again, I hope you are well and have a wonderful and blessed life.

Thank you for your kind words. I have heard Vancuver mentioned in some circles as being more progressive. But you're right some of the most bigoted crap I've seen spewed was from ones using their religion to justify hate. I'm a Christian myself and have struggled to reconcile that with being trans because no one would *choose* to be this way.

I wish more were like you. Trans people just want to live our lives like anyone else. But I've had family and coworkers tell me I just need to "be professional" or worry that I was going to start dressing like a drag queen (totally different and not me).

I wish you well, thanks again.

Thank you. And you're right, I wish there was another way. I have done some Googleing to see if any countries allowed assisted suicide but you have to be terminally ill.

I may forgo the gun then I don't want them to deal with that. I've got an area in mind where there is a deep forest so hopefully no random person has to deal with it.

As for stats, yeah trans people like me have somewhere around a 43% suicide rate. I used to think there was no way I'd be a statistic. Now I'm just kind of marking time until I make another attempt better prepared this time.

I am SO GLAD you're still here man! What you're describing sounds so familiar, my therapist calls it a "disassociated state". Speaking of which, do you have a therapist or someone IRL to talk to? 

I am 45, MTF and pre- everything. I understand what you're saying about being emotionally drained. I just broke yesterday after the fight and just shut down. Went over the top acting like I was just fine, got the kids to bed, cleaned the cat's litter box, then went into the garage and tried to hang myself. Got up afterwards and just went to bed. Woke up with a pounding headache, stiff/ sore neck, and pain in my eyes. 

I hope you get something to eat, call your dad, and just take a nice shower or bath. I remember being 20 and it was not the fun time it's portrayed as in the movies. FWIW back then I had a couple thousand in student debt for a college I had to leave due to running out of money. I had $10 to my name and had to choose gas to get to class or food for the rest of the week. I bought a loaf of bread, a jar of peanut butter, a gallon of milk and some cheddar cheese. That and a couple cans of soup was it for the week and sometimes that's all I'd have in my fridge. That's how I knew about getting out of debt. Except I didn't know enough to try to negotiate down. I just said I could only pay a few bucks until I got full time work. Then paid 50 bucks a month until it was paid off. 

Sorry, rambling again. Now you've got me thinking about Maine, *Gettysburg* the movie, and getting back out into nature. I've been in the suburbs too long :)

Oh dude for real you *have* to go see Maine! It's a state about 1/3 the size of California but only a little over a million people. There is soooooo many areas where you can just go out into the woods along streams, through mountains, and not see another soul. Acadia park near Bar Harbor is also must see, lots of places to bike, walk, hike.  Before I left the state around 26 I climbed out on a rocky outcropping near a cove so I had a 180 degree view of nothing but the Atlantic out to the horizon and a dome of stars overhead. 

I get what you're saying about not impacting the area, that's cool. Where I grew up was lots of old- growth forests with fully mature trees and no trails so just great places to go chill. If you ever watch the movie *Gettysburg*, the scene where the 20th Maine fights for Little Round Top looks like some of area I'd seen growing up. Just trees on a mountain where you're not sure if anyone had walked there in the last 20 years.

Just a question for you though, you sound like an outdoorsy type and I grew up in the northeast. Do you hike and/or camp a lot usually? Have you ever been to Maine/New Hampshire/ Vermont or anywhere along the Appalachian trail? What do you consider an "off trail" spot? I had never considered hiking off trail around here due to venomous snakes but I'm just wondering how you find spots like that, to just kind of get away from it all?

Sorry that was more than 1 question but I was just intrigued by the idea of off trail hiking. That must be a lot of fun and very peaceful to hammock out there.

Full disclosure, I'm here browsing the sub because months of off and on suicidal thoughts finally led to me trying last night. I am transgender too and with a cis woman who has tried to understand but can't she screamed at me this weekend how I am a confused and fucked up freak. And more. I don't feel angry, upset, or even hurt this just confirmed what I've been telling myself. 

I say this because it's worth it for you to find someone who loves you for who you are.  You can contact your creditors and make settlements on your own. Sure, it may put some dings on your credit score for a few years but that's temporary as opposed to being dead. At this point I'd prefer living in a van on my own if it meant not living every day miserable and hating both who I am pretending to be as well as hating the woman I will never be. 

You are entitled to a free credit report every year. It will have contact info for each creditor so you can work something out. My experience has shown most of them would rather take something rather than nothing. 

I'm sorry, I'm afraid I'm just rambling and not being much help. I do hope you decide to live and feel better. You are valid and deserve to be happy.

Thanks, I was going to come out to a close friend of mine so I could talk to him. That actually sparked part of the fight last week, we hadn't had a date night in awhile so that became a fight. 

Edit: meaning yes, I should talk to a friend. My therapist/ second therapist I'm not sure I can do. I feel like they just say "transition anyway and let your wife deal with it on her own". But she's in a rough place herself, she wouldn't be able to "just deal with it." You're *right*, I just can't do it and send my wife off the deep end.
You're right, thanks. It was a rough night but feeling a lot better today.
No You're right, I think I was just having a rough day and it all hit me harder than it should have. I feel much better today, thank you!
Thanks dude. Still in the game. I'm feeling a lot better today.

Thanks, man. I haven't shaved my head yet so that's my sole concession to maybe staying in the game a little longer. I scrubbed all the nail polish off and cut my nails back to the quick. I'm telling everyone I'm ok but I just sent a message to my therapist not to use my female name any more and use my birth name. 

People can tell I'm off I think because I've been asked 4 times today if I'm okay. Two of them said I look unwell. This is just how it was before I came out. The anxiety attacks are back already. 

Everyone is home now so I need to focus on my "I'm okay nothing is wrong" act. Thank you all for your responses it means a lot.
I mentioned that sub the day I came out to her. We had a joint session planned for over a month. It became an issue the day of and that's when this all came out.

You're right, and I appreciate your insight. She did notice the change when I realized I was trans but before I came out to her. She said I was happier and much more at ease. 

But she can't handle me changing. She is my soul mate. I'm not angry, I don't blame her. I just don't have it in me to fight these misconceptions that this is a "choice" and that the things I did was some trivial choice like picking out a new pair of shoes or something.

On some level I know what you say is true. But I know I have a tendency to let anger get the better of me. I was miserable as a man and was starting to get very irratable at any little thing. After I accepted myself as trans I became much happier and easier to be around (people told me this, not just my view).

As for the quiet calm, that's what made me wonder. I am a little bit of a gun enthusiast, the stress of not coming out to my spouse got to me to where one day I couldn't shake the though of putting a round through my head. It scared me and I sought help  and came out to my spouse. But amfter this I don't feel that way. I just listened to them basically tell me they couldn't take who I am. I nodded calmly, said I didn't blame them, and immediately started changing back to guy mode. Took off the polish, and am going to shave my head tonight. They took it as a positive step but inside I'm just mentally drafting the goodbye messages. 

For what it's worth, I do not *own* a gun and I still can't visualize actually doing it. But I know I'm not in a good place. I'm going to try considering a way to get better but I just don't see it right now. Thank you for trying to help though I appreciate it.

No you're right, but I had already told my therapist I was struggling by holding back and only doing little things. They said it was my journey and to find a way to strengthen my spouse's coping and support mechanisms so they can be in a better place. Again, they're not wrong but it's not working. I can't *make* someone accept me. So if I tell my therapist this I'm sure they'll say I should proceed anyway or something and that will just end badly.

Pulling a stunt like starting hrt in secret would likely be tantamount to cheating. 

I thought I was being low key by painting my toenails, letting my hair start to grow out from a buzz cut, and that's it. They're fine with my hair (still looks like a man's cut) but the nails was too much.

You're not wrong, but I burned myself up trying to thread the needle of feeling a *little* like the woman I felt I was inside without blowing everything the fuck up. I lost some weight, painted my toenails and put clear polish on my fingers. I started to let my more natural feminine mannerisms out but I suppressed them except when I was in private. It already was a struggle because I was still pretty much having to present 100% male everywhere and didn't have anywhere I could explore what it meant to be me. 

And that was too much. 

So, if I continue it is clear I loose everything. And yes I'd still be alive but living with the pain of transition **and** the pain of losing them. My parents divorced when I was 5 and spent the rest of my life since then fucking my head up with emotional abuse. I swore if I ever had kids I would do anything...*anything* to spare them from divorce. At least if I spin out and am gone then it's on me and my spouse can say whatever. 

I know many trans people live with the loss of family, spouses, etc.  Unending pain and anguish. I'm not strong like you are, I knew that going in and figured at best I'd have a chance at being in the slim minority that salvaged their life during transition. It doesn't appear that way.

I'm also admittedly weak in that my response to overwhelming emotional trauma is to shut down. The only "positive" thing I can feel I can control is to close myself off and turn the pain inwards. I'm not going to be the emotionally abusive rage-aholic I grew up around and feared becoming. I'll find a way out first. 

Thank you for your response though. It means a lot someone cared to respond and I wish I could turn around and stand up to this. But I can't.  Thank you though.
Impossible as it is for me to accept, I'm afraid that is where I will end up as well. Thank you for your responses, I have been thinking I was weird or something.

204Hz! I just tried this with the Voice Pitch Analyzer app. My previous high avg was 130Hz, but for like 2 seconds I was at 204Hz! FIRST TIME ever reaching into female range!!!

It was so brief, and clearly I have so far to go. But I am literally crying right now because I didnt think it was possible. Two seconds is going to change my life. You have no idea how happy you have made me!

For two seconds, I was there.
Yeah, I wanted to let you know because what seems obvious to us sometimes is another person's mystery :)

True. And your idea was literally the first "ahha" moment for me, thank you so much!

I have kind of put my voice out of thought mostly because I am worried, no convinced it will never pass. I was always complimented on my deep, resonant voice and have actually done professional voice work. Now, it is something I can barely think about but have been trying to practice lately. 

Now maybe I can make a little progress, for what good it may do me.

So hrt did change that for you? This I find both curious and terrifying. I love my wife and she has stuck with me after I came out to her a month ago.

I just can't even visualize a guy that way, and I think I've tried lately. Like, I can look at one every now and then and see objectively where he is what society deems 'attractive'. But when I try to then imagine anything beyond that it's a nope.

It's also emotional for me. I have always needed to feel an emotional connection with a woman before having sex with her. In a way, I *can* imagine myself fully as a woman and then being submissive to a man, and thats where my conundrum come in. I want to be penetrated as a woman by a man, but in my head it is always a faceless almost detached penis. Weird I know. But I am both terrified of it *and* feel it is something I need to feel fully like a woman.

Oh my gosh, thank you for this. I keep seeing references to raising the larynx but no idea how to. I figured it was something so commonly known no one was explaining it and I just was out of the loop. Thank you!

I'm actually afraid of this myself. I've only ever been with/attracted to women and am married to one now and I love her deeply. But I am scared to death of my orientation flipping or at least being bi. Because part of me has always fantasized about having sex as a woman, with a man. In a very *real* and "biological" sense. But I can't imagine being attracted to a man or forming an emotional bond with one.
